subject: Convert accelerator stipend to committed discount for GlowLab
messages:
From: Ava Cole <ava@glowlab.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@glowlab.com
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Convert accelerator stipend to committed discount?

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the seed-stage credits you provided through the Lighthouse accelerator — they9ve been huge for our infra tests. Procurement is now asking whether we can fold the remaining promo stipend into a pricing commitment for Dedicated capacity as part of our contract review.

Quick context: we have ~$30,000 of unused accelerator credits that would otherwise expire at end-of-quarter. Our procurement/legal team prefers a committed discount (so it shows on the PO/SOW) rather than line-item credits.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood convert promotional credits into a time-bound committed discount (e.g., 3-6 months) on Dedicated capacity?
- If yes, what would the billing/proration and SOW language look like (procurement wants a line item they can PO against)?

Procurement is on a short cadence and would like a proposed approach this week. I attached a short note with the current credit balance and our target usage profile (glowlab_request.pdf).

Appreciate your help — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Ava
Ava Cole
Head of Platform, GlowLab Inc
ava@glowlab.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ava Cole <ava@glowlab.com>
Cc: procurement@glowlab.com, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Convert accelerator stipend to committed discount?

Hi Ava — thanks for the note and the attachment. Short answer: we can make this work, but there are two paths we typically use and I wanted to outline both so procurement can pick the right fit quickly.

Option A — Credit conversion to one-time invoice credit: we apply the $30k as a pre-paid credit on the account and convert to an invoice line that reduces charges until exhausted. Minimal legal work, but credits don9t show as a committed discount on a PO. Prorated mid-month.

Option B — Convert to time-bound committed discount on Dedicated (preferred for procurement): we convert the economic value of the credits into a discount (percent off list) for a set term (3-6 months) with a minimum committed monthly spend. Requires an amendment to the order form / SOW so procurement can PO against it. There are a few finance/legal checks (rev recognition, tax).

If you9re okay, I9ll loop in Finance/Legal and propose a term sheet. Can you confirm whether the credits must appear on the PO (procurement preference) or if an account-level credit is acceptable? I9ll also propose a proration approach if they want a mid-month start.

I9ve CC9d Rishi to help with term modeling — we can get a one-pager back by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: GlowLab - request to convert $30k accelerator credits to committed discount (need exception)

Team —

GlowLab (DL-8721) reached out asking to convert ~$30k of expiring accelerator credits into a committed discount on a Dedicated capacity contract so procurement can PO the line item. Procurement specifically wants an amendment/SOW entry rather than an account credit.

Proposed commercial carve:
- Convert $30,000 of promo credit into an equivalent economic discount spread over 6 months (starts on activation of Dedicated)
- Minimum committed spend: $5,000/mo during that period (GlowLab expects usage > this)
- Economic effect: roughly 20% off committed capacity in months 1-6 vs list rates (exact % depends on capacity SKU mix)
- Proration: start date prorated to first day of the month of activation; unused portion of credits consumed as one-time credit if they terminate early

Questions / asks for exception approval:
1) Finance — confirm whether converting promo credits to an explicit discount term is acceptable for revenue recognition (does it force deferral?) and any tax implications. I attached a sketch term sheet (proposed_term_sheet.pdf) and a quick cost model (cost_model.xlsx).
2) Legal — will need simple amendment language to add a line in SOW showing the discount value and term.
3) GTM/CS — if approved, we need DocuSign-ready SOW language and an onboarding window (CS to schedule) so usage ramps into the committed months.

If we can agree today I9ll propose this to Ava and procurement and include a DocuSign link.

Thanks —
Ben

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T11:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: GlowLab - request to convert $30k accelerator credits to committed discount (need exception)

Ben — good framing. A couple of thoughts from pricing/finance:

- Rather than a straight dollar-for-dollar conversion, recommend we offer a hybrid: convert $25k of the credit into an 18% committed discount over 5 months with a $6k minimum monthly commitment. Hold $5k as an onboarding/top-up credit to be applied during month 1 only (helps adoption). This preserves some incentive for usage and reduces churn risk.
- Finance: we can treat the discount as a commercial concession; it will require an adjustment in revenue recognition (deferral) but it9s manageable if we document it as an amendment. Please confirm in writing.
- Legal: ensure SOW language clarifies "one-time conversion of accelerator stipend to committed discount" and includes a clause for early termination proration.

I9ve linked the HubSpot record for context: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-8702 (GlowLab opportunity). I9ve attached a quick workbook showing the monthly P&L impact (cost_model.xlsx).

If Marissa is comfortable with the concession, I9ll draft a short term-sheet and a DocuSign-ready amendment.

-Rishi
Director, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: GlowLab - request to convert $30k accelerator credits to committed discount (need exception)

Thanks for the back-and-forth. I approve a one-time exception with the following guardrails:

- Convert $25,000 of accelerator credit into a time-bound committed discount equal to ~18% off standard Dedicated pricing for 5 months.
- Set a $6,000/month minimum committed spend for the 5-month period.
- Retain $5,000 as a month-1 onboarding credit (applied to month 1 invoice only).
- Proration: discount term starts on the first day of the month following activation; if GlowLab terminates early, any unconsumed discount value is forfeited (or used as a final invoice credit at Finance9s discretion).

Next steps:
1) Ben — send the proposed term-sheet to Ava and procurement and ask them to confirm PO language preference (we can either include a dollar value line item or phrase as "% committed discount applied to SKU list" in SOW).
2) Legal — please draft a short amendment and SOW entry. I9ve attached a template SOW for redline (GlowLab_SOW_Sept2027.pdf).
3) CS/Onboarding — schedule a kickoff within 7 business days of signed amendment; apply the $5k onboarding credit on first invoice.

I9m okay with the HubSpot note and DocuSign flow. Finance, please confirm the rev-rec approach once legal finalizes language.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
